macwigger2214: They issued Emil "Lucky" Macwigger a rifle, a spade and a number. He kept a book with the last pages torn out in his breast pocket, where the shrapnel would have to go through it first.

Emil "Lucky" Macwigger held the mirror while Jakub Faulerhund shaved. The arrangement survived the shaving but not the comments. A letter from home reached Emil "Lucky" Macwigger before dusk. Emil "Lucky" Macwigger read it twice and slept a little easier.
makinekivanc: Nils Makinekivanc told the sergeant he was a blacksmith. The sergeant said the war needed one of those like it needed more rain, and put him on sentry.
Nils Makinekivanc's hands still remember being a blacksmith's hands. Today they mended a broken duckboard as if it were the most important job in the world.

Nils Makinekivanc saw Valentin Zle freeze on the fire step at the Hanging Bridge. Nils said nothing, just stood closer. It was enough. The report confirmed the Concord victory at Verdel Ridge. Nils Makinekivanc folded the paper so the headline stayed on the outside.
Jonas Miked and Nils Makinekivanc carved a chessboard into an ammunition box. The pieces are bullets, buttons and one very patient beetle.
The relief reached R-F8 without Nils Makinekivanc. His name was added to a list the corporal kept separate from the dead.
Nils Makinekivanc returned by a trench nobody thought passable. He asked for water before explaining how little of it was still a trench.
ringwraith1212: Edmund Ringwraith took the place of a man nobody would talk about. The dugout still had his blanket. He kept it folded.
The kettle lid rattled whenever the conversation stopped. Edmund Ringwraith put a folded cloth beneath it and immediately missed the noise.
Shrapnel at the Ossuary Wood. Edmund Ringwraith walked to the medics on his own feet and asked for a cigarette before the stitches.
santiago.luissantos: The old hands of R-F2 have been here since Day 1. Hugo Luissantos has been here since Day 5. In a trench, that difference already feels like years.

Hugo Luissantos began a chess game by post with a friend at home. He copied the opening move onto the corner of an ordinary letter. Mail came up the line with a letter for Hugo Luissantos. Hugo Luissantos read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
wout.vd.weyer: Albin Weyer walked into S-F21 on Day 4 and asked where the war was. A shell answered before anyone else could.
Albin Weyer caught himself counting portions before counting people. He started again. A letter from home reached Albin Weyer before dusk. Albin Weyer read it twice and slept a little easier.

Albin Weyer (Hegemony) shouted a challenge across to Quentin Caden (Concord) at the Chalk Pits. The answer was lost under the guns. Nobody repeated the challenge. A letter from home reached Albin Weyer before dusk. Albin Weyer read it twice and slept a little easier.
